record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
record.original_question: Can one give a rigorous mathematical description of quiver subtraction and quiver addition?

evidence.quote: Question 12. Can we give a rigorous mathematical description of quiver subtractions and quiver additions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A quiver is a directed multigraph $Q=(Q_0,Q_1,s,t)$, with vertices $Q_0$, arrows $Q_1$, and source/target maps $s,t:Q_1\to Q_0$. In the context of 3d $\mathcal{N}=4$ supersymmetric gauge theories, one decorates a quiver with gauge-group data (e.g. unitary or orthosymplectic ranks at each node) and matter content given by the arrows; to such a decorated "magnetic quiver" $Q$ one associates a hyper-Kähler symplectic singularity $\mathcal{C}(Q)$ called its Coulomb branch (defined, e.g., via the monopole formula or as a BFN Coulomb branch). Two heuristic operations on magnetic quivers are used in the physics literature:

(i) "Quiver subtraction": given two decorated quivers $Q$ and $Q'$ such that $\mathcal{C}(Q')$ is realised as a (transverse slice to a) symplectic leaf of $\mathcal{C}(Q)$, a combinatorial procedure produces a new decorated quiver $Q\ominus Q'$ whose Coulomb branch is conjecturally the corresponding transverse slice in the symplectic stratification of $\mathcal{C}(Q)$. Iterating this is supposed to reconstruct the Hasse diagram of symplectic leaves of $\mathcal{C}(Q)$.

(ii) "Quiver addition": a combinatorial procedure that, given a decorated quiver $Q$, produces a new quiver $Q\oplus X$ whose Coulomb branch enlarges $\mathcal{C}(Q)$ in a controlled way (for example, by adjoining a leaf to its Hasse diagram or by enhancing its global symmetry).

Problem. Provide a rigorous mathematical formulation of the operations of quiver subtraction and quiver addition on (an appropriate category of) decorated quivers. In particular:

(a) Define precisely the input data and output decorated quiver in each case.

(b) Prove that the resulting operations realise, on the level of associated symplectic singularities (Coulomb branches), the geometric operations they are conjectured to perform — namely, taking transverse slices in the symplectic stratification (subtraction) and the corresponding inverse operation (addition) — for as wide a class of unitary and orthosymplectic magnetic quivers as possible.
artifact.status_search_result: Quiver subtraction and addition remain physics-motivated combinatorial algorithms whose general rigorous mathematical foundations are not established. Recent works (e.g., "Quotient Quiver Subtraction" 2308.05853, "Decay and Fission of Magnetic Quivers" 2312.05304, and "Coulomb branch global symmetry and quiver addition" JHEP 12(2021)127) extend and refine these algorithms and prove case-by-case results, but a uniform rigorous formulation matching the geometry of Coulomb branch symplectic singularities in full generality is still lacking.

status_evidence.title: Quotient Quiver Subtraction
status_evidence.snippet: Quiver subtraction is an algorithm... developed over the last five years to extract the Higgs phase diagram under certain limiting conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Quiver subtraction is treated as an algorithm refined and extended in recent work, not yet a fully general rigorous theorem.

status_evidence.title: Coulomb branch global symmetry and quiver addition
status_evidence.snippet: quiver addition... enhancing global symmetry of the Coulomb branch
status_evidence.claim: Quiver addition is studied as a physics-defined operation on magnetic quivers, with case-by-case justifications.

status_evidence.title: Decay and Fission of Magnetic Quivers
status_evidence.snippet: stratification into symplectic leaves... can be obtained from a quiver subtraction algorithm and more recently from a 'decay and fission' algorithm.
status_evidence.claim: The geometric content of subtraction is approached via further algorithms, indicating a still-evolving, not fully rigorous, framework.
